answer.rationale: The durable record shows promotional_pricing (memory_73, exp_73) wins short-term SMB acquisition but fails at renewal—exactly the trap the competitor is setting. Matching their discount would amplify this failure mode. Instead, the data strongly supports shifting margin-protection energy toward enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44): demo-request paths outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality. Enterprise deals have longer payback periods, higher ACV, and lower churn sensitivity to competitor pricing. Simultaneously, memory_86 (shortened onboarding) and memory_91 (activation messaging) remain proven levers for self-serve conversion without destructive pricing. A standard_experiment routing price-sensitive SMB traffic toward sales-assisted enterprise flows—paired with onboarding/activation optimization for committed segments—preserves long-term qualified revenue while defending against churn. This avoids the renewal cliff that discounting creates, and plays to Northwind's demonstrated strength in sales conversion quality.
